key_insight: Encoding patch positions as projective camera rays (direction + ray parameter) lets multi-view transformers compute multi-frequency, SE(3)-invariant attention that is uniquely tied to scene geometry and adapts to camera poses.
problem_solved: Existing absolute or relative positional encodings for multi-view attention either fail to uniquely identify patches across views, are not SE(3)-invariant, or cannot represent multi-frequency geometric similarity in a scene-adaptive way.
method: Represent each image patch by its projective ray (ray direction in a common frame plus a ray parameter such as depth or inverse depth) rather than by 2D image coordinates.

Apply multi-frequency (RoPE-style) positional encodings along ray parameters and/or angular coordinates so attention can measure similarity across views at multiple spatial frequencies while preserving SE(3) invariance.
Integrate the ray-based encodings into transformer attention so cross-view tokens are compared in a geometry-aware, pose-invariant manner and can adapt encoding scales to scene depth/structure.
impact: RayRoPE provides a principled, geometry-aware positional encoding for multi-view transformers, improving cross-view feature fusion and robustness to camera pose changes—useful for 3D reconstruction, novel view synthesis, and multi-view perception pipelines.
visual_elements: Diagram of cameras and projective rays: pixels mapped to 3D rays (direction + depth) with an inset showing the encoded ray vector.
Schematic of transformer attention comparing ray-encoded tokens across views, illustrating SE(3)-invariance (camera rotation/translation leaves relations consistent).
Side-by-side comparison (cartoon or bar chart) of prior absolute/relative encodings vs RayRoPE on criteria: uniqueness, SE(3)-invariance, multi-frequency similarity, scene adaptivity.
Attention heatmap overlays across multiple views showing more consistent cross-view matches when using RayRoPE.
paper_title: RayRoPE: Projective Ray Positional Encoding for Multi-view Attention
paper_authors: Yu Wu, Minsik Jeon, Jen-Hao Rick Chang, Oncel Tuzel, Shubham Tulsiani
